For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.
sql:
WITH shortest_streak AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT CAST(insert_date AS DATE) as date_entry
    FROM cities
    WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
      AND insert_date LIKE '2021-07%'
),
ranked_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        date_entry,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY date_entry) as rn,
        LAG(date_entry, 1) OVER (ORDER BY date_entry) as prev_date,
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_date IS NULL OR date_entry != prev_date + INTERVAL 1 DAY
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END as is_gap
    FROM shortest_streak
),
streak_id AS (
    SELECT 
        date_entry,
        rn,
        SUM(is_gap) OVER (ORDER BY rn) as streak_start_rn
    FROM ranked_dates
),
streaks AS (
    SELECT 
        date_entry,
        rn,
        streak_start_rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY streak_start_rn) as streak_length
    FROM streak_id
),
streak_summary AS (
    SELECT 
        streak_length,
        streak_start_rn,
        MIN(date_entry) as first_date,
        MAX(date_entry) as last_date
    FROM streaks
    GROUP BY streak_length, streak_start_rn
)
SELECT 
    streak_length,
    first_date,
    last_date
FROM streak_summary
ORDER BY streak_length DESC, first_date
